motor_vehicles_act_1988.last_amended: Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 (effective 01-09-2019); Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023
motor_vehicles_act_1988.objective: To consolidate and amend the law relating to motor vehicles, regulate road transport, ensure road safety, and provide for licensing, registration, insurance, and penalties.

chapters.title: Preliminary
chapters.description: Short title, extent, commencement, and definitions of key terms.

chapters.title: Licensing of Drivers of Motor Vehicles
chapters.description: Rules governing driving licences — learner's, permanent, renewal, disqualification, endorsement.

chapters.title: Licensing of Conductors of Stage Carriages
chapters.description: Grant, revocation, and disqualification of conductor licences.

chapters.title: Registration of Motor Vehicles
chapters.description: Registration requirements, certificates, suspension, cancellation, and maintenance of state registers.

chapters.title: Control of Transport Vehicles
chapters.description: Permits for stage carriages, contract carriages, goods vehicles; duration, transfer, cancellation.

chapters.title: Special Provisions Relating to State Transport Undertakings
chapters.description: Schemes for road transport undertakings, permits, and compensation.

chapters.title: Construction, Equipment and Maintenance of Motor Vehicles
chapters.description: General standards for vehicle construction, equipment, and maintenance — delegated to Central Government rules.

chapters.title: Control of Traffic
chapters.description: Speed limits, weight limits, traffic signs, driving regulations, duties of drivers at accidents.

chapters.title: Motor Vehicles Temporarily Leaving or Visiting India
chapters.description: Rules for foreign vehicles operating in or temporarily entering India.

chapters.title: Liability Without Fault in Certain Cases
chapters.description: No-fault liability of vehicle owner — compensation for death/disability without proving negligence.

chapters.title: Insurance of Motor Vehicles Against Third Party Risks
chapters.description: Mandatory third-party insurance, requirements of policies, rights of third parties, hit-and-run compensation.

chapters.title: Claims Tribunals
chapters.description: Establishment, procedure, and powers of Motor Accident Claims Tribunals (MACTs).

chapters.title: Offences, Penalties and Procedure
chapters.description: Comprehensive list of traffic offences and corresponding penalties.

chapters.title: Miscellaneous
chapters.description: Miscellaneous powers of authorities, protection, and enforcement.

key_sections.title: Necessity for Driving Licence
key_sections.description: No person shall drive a motor vehicle in any public place unless he holds an effective driving licence. Applicable to all vehicle categories.

key_sections.title: Age Limit for Driving
key_sections.description: Minimum age 18 years for a permanent licence. Learner's permit available from 16 years for non-transport vehicles.

key_sections.title: Responsibility of Owners
key_sections.description: Vehicle owners are responsible for ensuring their vehicle is not driven by persons contravening Sections 3 or 4.

key_sections.title: Grant of Learner's Licence
key_sections.description: Procedure for issuance of learner's licence including medical certificate and test requirements.

key_sections.title: Grant of Driving Licence
key_sections.description: Procedure for issuance of permanent driving licence after passing the required driving test.

key_sections.title: Necessity for Registration
key_sections.description: No person shall drive or allow a motor vehicle to be driven on public roads without a valid registration certificate.

key_sections.title: Registration — How to be Made
key_sections.description: Vehicle registration procedure with the RTO. Registration certificate valid for 15 years from date of registration (per 2019 amendment).

key_sections.title: Certificate of Fitness of Transport Vehicles
key_sections.description: Transport vehicles must hold a valid fitness certificate issued by the testing authority.

key_sections.title: Limits of Speed
key_sections.description: State Government may prescribe speed limits for different vehicle categories on different road types. Violation is punishable under Section 183.

key_sections.title: Limits of Weight and Limitations on Use
key_sections.description: Prescribes maximum axle weight and Gross Vehicle Weight for different vehicle types.

key_sections.title: Power to Erect Traffic Signs
key_sections.description: Authorities empowered to erect traffic signs and signals. All drivers must obey traffic signs per Section 119.

key_sections.title: Duty to Obey Traffic Signs
key_sections.description: Every driver must obey directions given by traffic signs and signals.

key_sections.title: Wearing of Protective Headgear
key_sections.description: Mandatory helmet wearing for drivers and pillion riders of two-wheelers. BIS/ISI-marked helmets required.

key_sections.title: Duty to Produce Licence and Certificate of Registration
key_sections.description: Driver must carry and produce driving licence and registration certificate on demand by a police officer.

key_sections.title: Duty of Driver in Case of Accident
key_sections.description: Driver involved in an accident must stop, give assistance, and report to police. Failure to carry injured to hospital is punishable.

key_sections.title: No-Fault Liability
key_sections.description: Compensation on no-fault basis: Rs. 50,000 for death; Rs. 25,000 for permanent disability.

key_sections.title: Necessity for Insurance Against Third Party Risk
key_sections.description: Every motor vehicle on public roads must be covered by at minimum a valid third-party insurance policy.

key_sections.title: Compensation in Case of Hit-and-Run Motor Accident
key_sections.description: Special compensation scheme for victims of accidents where vehicle and driver cannot be identified. Now governed by Scheme 2022.

key_sections.title: Claims Tribunals
key_sections.description: State Governments shall constitute Motor Accident Claims Tribunals for adjudicating compensation claims.

key_sections.title: Application for Compensation
key_sections.description: Accident victims or their legal representatives may file claims before the MACT for compensation.

central_motor_vehicles_rules_1989.objective: To implement the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 with respect to driving licences, registration, construction and maintenance of vehicles, and vehicle standards.

chapters.title: Preliminary (Rules 1-2)
chapters.description: Short title, commencement, and definitions including vehicle categories (M1, M2, M3, N1, N2, N3, L categories).

chapters.title: Licensing of Drivers (Rules 3-33)
chapters.description: Forms, tests, medical requirements, endorsements, and procedures for all types of driving licences.

chapters.title: Licensing of Conductors (Rules 34-45)
chapters.description: Rules for granting and managing conductor licences for stage carriages.

chapters.title: Registration of Motor Vehicles (Rules 46-88)
chapters.description: Registration procedures, registration marks, transfer of ownership, fitness certificates for transport vehicles.

chapters.title: Control of Transport Vehicles (Rules 89-100)
chapters.description: Permit conditions, stage carriage, contract carriage, goods carriage permit requirements.

chapters.title: Construction, Equipment and Maintenance (Rules 101-124)
chapters.description: Detailed technical standards for brakes, tyres, lighting, dimensions, exhaust emissions, safety devices.

chapters.title: Control of Traffic (Rules 125-138)
chapters.description: Traffic signs, speed limits, parking, driving regulations, safety belts, child restraints.

chapters.title: Insurance (Rules 139-143)
chapters.description: Procedures for insurance documentation and third-party policy requirements.

chapters.title: Claims Tribunals (Rules 144-163)
chapters.description: Procedures for filing claims before Motor Accident Claims Tribunals.

chapters.title: Miscellaneous (Rules 164+)
chapters.description: Additional rules on vehicle standards, registration of dealers, and enforcement.

key_rules.title: Definitions — Vehicle Categories
key_rules.description: M1: Passenger vehicle up to 8 seats; M2/M3: Buses; N1/N2/N3: Goods vehicles by GVW; L category: 2 and 3 wheelers. Agricultural tractor also defined.

key_rules.title: Learner's Licence — Driving Test
key_rules.description: Applicant must pass a test on traffic signs and basic driving.

key_rules.title: Medical Certificate Requirements
key_rules.description: Form 1 for non-transport vehicles (self-declaration); Form 1-A medical certificate from Civil Surgeon for transport vehicle licences.

key_rules.title: Speed Limits — Central Notification
key_rules.description: Implements Section 112 speed limits. Base notification S.O. 1522(E) dated 6 April 2018 fixed national maximum limits.

key_rules.title: Safety Measures for Children on Motorcycles
key_rules.description: Amended Feb 2022: Prescribes safety norms for carriage of children below 4 years on motorcycles.

rules_of_road_regulations_1989.objective: To govern the conduct of drivers and road users while using public roads in India.

rules.title: Keep Left
rules.description: All motor vehicles must keep to the left side of the road and allow traffic to pass on the right.

rules.title: Overtaking
rules.description: Overtake only from the right side, when safe. Do not overtake (a) near bends/corners/hills, (b) when the vehicle ahead is near an intersection, (c) if following vehicle has begun overtaking, (d) if driver ahead has not signalled consent.

rules.title: Prohibition on Preventing Overtaking
rules.description: When being overtaken, do not increase speed or interfere with the overtaking vehicle.

rules.title: Slowing Down at Intersections
rules.description: Drivers must slow down when approaching road intersections, junctions, pedestrian crossings, and road corners.

rules.title: Safe Following Distance
rules.description: Maintain sufficient distance from the vehicle ahead to avoid collision if it suddenly slows or stops.

rules.title: Gradual Braking
rules.description: Do not apply brakes abruptly unless absolutely necessary to avoid accidents.

rules.title: Towing Speed Limit
rules.description: No motor vehicle towing another vehicle (other than a trailer or sidecar) shall exceed 24 km/h.

rules.title: Pedestrian Crossings
rules.description: Drivers must slow down and give way to pedestrians at marked pedestrian crossings.

rules.title: Obedience to Traffic Directions
rules.description: All drivers must obey: (a) police officer signals, (b) traffic signs/notices, (c) automatic traffic signals at intersections.

rules.title: Right of Way at Junctions
rules.description: At uncontrolled junctions, give way to vehicles approaching from the right.

rules.title: Prohibition on Footpaths
rules.description: Motor vehicles must not be driven on footpaths or cycle tracks without permission of an on-duty police officer.

rules.title: Lane Discipline
rules.description: Drive in designated lanes; do not straddle lanes or change lanes unnecessarily without signalling.

rules.title: Use of Horns
rules.description: Horn should be used only when necessary. Prohibited in silence zones (hospitals, schools).

rules.title: Headlights — Use at Night
rules.description: Use headlights from sunset to sunrise and in conditions of reduced visibility.

rules.title: Parking Restrictions
rules.description: No parking near traffic lights, on pedestrian crossings, footpaths, within 5 metres of an intersection, or where obstructing traffic.

rules.title: Signals Before Turning
rules.description: Mandatory to give hand or mechanical signals before turning, changing lanes, or stopping.

rules.title: Right Turn
rules.description: Position vehicle to the middle of road, make a broad progressive right turn.

rules.title: Left Turn
rules.description: Stay to the left side before making a left turn.

rules.title: U-Turn
rules.description: U-turns permitted only where traffic conditions allow safely and where not prohibited by signs.

rules.title: Speed at Junctions
rules.description: Approach intersections at reduced speed; do not enter until it is safe.

rules.title: Loaded Vehicles
rules.description: Drivers of heavily loaded vehicles must take extra care, particularly on slopes and narrow roads.

solatium_scheme_1989.superseded_by: Compensation to Victims of Hit and Run Motor Accidents Scheme, 2022 (GSR 163(E) dated 25.02.2022)
solatium_scheme_1989.objective: To provide fixed compensation to victims of hit-and-run motor accidents where the responsible vehicle cannot be identified.

death.note: Revised from Rs. 25,000 at inception; last revised 1994

current_scheme_2022.name: Compensation to Victims of Hit and Run Motor Accidents Scheme, 2022
current_scheme_2022.fund: Motor Vehicle Accident Fund (Hit and Run Compensation Account)
current_scheme_2022.initial_corpus: Rs. 76.28 Crore transferred from erstwhile Solatium Fund (New India Assurance)

claim_procedure.settles_at: Claims Settlement Commissioner (District Collector / Deputy Commissioner)
claim_procedure.timeline: Payment within 15 days from receipt of Claims Enquiry Officer report

rent_a_cab_scheme_1989.objective: To regulate the business of renting motor cabs (taxis) to the public on a time or mileage basis.
key_provisions: Operators must obtain a Rent-a-Cab licence from the State Transport Authority.
Cab must be a motor vehicle not plying for hire as a stage carriage.
Minimum fleet requirement may be prescribed by state authorities.
Vehicles must be maintained in roadworthy condition and carry all valid documents.
Driver must hold a valid driving licence with authorisation to drive transport vehicles.
Fare or rate schedule must be displayed in the vehicle.
Operator liable for acts of driver while vehicle is on hire.
Insurance coverage as required under Section 146 of MVA 1988 is mandatory.

rent_a_motorcycle_scheme_1997.objective: To provide a regulatory framework for the business of renting motorcycles/two-wheelers to the public.
key_provisions: Operators must obtain a licence from competent authority under this scheme.
Motorcycles must be registered and have valid insurance.
Renter must hold a valid driving licence for two-wheelers.
Operator must ensure helmets are available for riders.
Operator liable for ensuring vehicle fitness before handing over.
Records of all hirings must be maintained by operator for inspection.
Applicable to all two-wheelers rented on time or mileage basis.

tourist_transport_permit_rules_1993.short_title: Motor Vehicles (All India Permit for Tourist Transport Operators) Rules, 1993
tourist_transport_permit_rules_1993.objective: To regulate the grant of All-India Tourist Permits to transport operators for operating tourist vehicles across state borders.
key_provisions: Permits valid throughout India — vehicle can operate across all state boundaries.
Tourist vehicle must display a yellow board with black lettering and carry 'TOURIST' marking.
Operator must apply to the State Transport Authority of the home state.
Vehicle must be less than 8 years old at time of permit application.
Driver must hold a valid driving licence for transport vehicles.
Compulsory third-party insurance and fitness certificate required.
Permit valid for 5 years, renewable.
Permit fee structure set by Central Government.
Vehicle must be air-conditioned to qualify as a Tourist Vehicle.
Operator must carry a permit copy and all vehicle documents at all times.

driving_licence_exemption_rules_1992.objective: To specify categories of persons and vehicles exempted from the requirement of a driving licence under the Act.

exemptions.description: Persons driving motor vehicles belonging to the Central Government for defence purposes under Section 18 of MVA 1988 may hold a defence-issued driving licence.
Persons driving tractors or other agricultural vehicles exclusively for agricultural purposes within a farm or private land may be exempted.
Persons driving invalid carriages (vehicles for physically disabled persons) that do not exceed speeds of 16 km/h may be exempted from certain licence conditions.

lpg_motor_vehicles_order_2001.short_title: The Liquefied Petroleum Gas (Regulation of Use in Motor Vehicles) Order, 2001
lpg_motor_vehicles_order_2001.objective: To regulate the conversion and use of LPG as fuel in motor vehicles to ensure safety standards.
key_provisions: Only BIS-certified LPG kits conforming to IS 14611 may be fitted in motor vehicles.
Conversion must be done at an authorised retrofitting centre.
Vehicle owner must obtain an amended Registration Certificate reflecting LPG fuel.
LPG cylinders in vehicles must conform to IS 7312 and must be tested and recertified periodically.
Insurance policy must be updated to reflect LPG fuel usage.
Vehicle must pass a fitness inspection post-conversion.
Transport vehicles must obtain approval from the State Transport Authority.

high_security_registration_plates_order_.short_title: The Motor Vehicles (New High Security Registration Plates) Order, 2001
high_security_registration_plates_order_.objective: To standardise and enhance the security of vehicle registration plates across India to prevent counterfeiting.
key_provisions: All vehicles registered after notified date must be fitted with High Security Registration Plates (HSRP).
HSRP must contain: a chromium-based hologram, a laser-branded permanent identification number (PIN), a hot-stamped IND inscription, and retro-reflective sheeting.
Plates must be affixed with snap-lock non-removable bolts.
Plate dimensions and font standardised nationally — white background for private vehicles, yellow for commercial.
Plates must be manufactured by authorised suppliers only.
Third number plate with self-destructive hologram sticker to be pasted on windshield.
Violation of HSRP requirements is punishable under MVA 1988.

motor_transport_workers_act_1961.objective: To regulate the conditions of employment of motor transport workers employed in motor transport undertakings.
motor_transport_workers_act_1961.applicability: Motor transport undertakings employing 5 or more motor transport workers.

key_provisions.description: Every motor transport undertaking must be registered with the registering authority.
No worker shall work more than 8 hours a day and 48 hours a week. No driving for more than 5 hours without a rest break of at least 30 minutes.
Every worker entitled to an 8-hour rest period between two periods of duty.
Workers entitled to one day off per week.
Wages must be paid at fixed pay periods not exceeding one month. Wages must be disbursed on a working day.
Overtime pay at twice the ordinary rate for hours worked beyond normal working hours.
Employer must ensure clean and adequate rest rooms, drinking water, canteens, and first-aid facilities.
Employer must provide uniforms, raincoats, and other protective equipment to workers.
Annual leave with wages at rate of 1 day for every 20 days of work in a calendar year.
One month notice required for termination of permanent workers.

fatal_accidents_act_1855.objective: To provide a right of action for wrongful death — enabling legal representatives of a deceased to sue for damages when a person's death is caused by the wrongful act, neglect or default of another.

key_provisions.title: Action for Wrongful Death
key_provisions.description: Whenever death is caused by wrongful act, neglect, or default that would have entitled the deceased to maintain an action for damages, the person's legal representatives may file suit for damages.

key_provisions.title: Parties Who May Sue
key_provisions.description: Only one action shall lie for and in respect of the same subject matter; it shall be for the benefit of wife, husband, parent, and child of the deceased person.

key_provisions.title: Assessment of Damages
key_provisions.description: Damages may include loss of financial support, loss of consortium, funeral expenses, and other losses arising from the death.

fatal_accidents_act_1855.relevance_to_traffic: Provides the historical basis for compensation claims in motor vehicle accident deaths, supplemented now by Chapter X and XII of MVA 1988.

public_liability_insurance_act_1991.objective: To provide for public liability insurance for the purpose of providing immediate relief to persons affected by accidents occurring while handling hazardous substances.

key_provisions.description: Every owner handling hazardous substances must take out an insurance policy against liability to give relief in case of death or injury to any person (other than an employee) or damage to property from an accident.
Immediate relief payable on no-fault basis: Rs. 25,000 for fatal accidents; Rs. 12,500 for permanent/total disability.
Claims to be filed before the Collector. Collector may pass award within 3 months.
Owner must also contribute to the Environmental Relief Fund.

public_liability_insurance_act_1991.relevance_to_traffic: Applies to vehicles transporting hazardous goods (tankers, chemical carriers). Supplements MVA 1988 Section 190(3) on carriage of dangerous goods.

road_transport_corporations_act_1950.objective: To provide for the establishment of Road Transport Corporations by State Governments for the efficient provision of road transport services.

key_provisions.description: State or Central Government may establish a Road Transport Corporation (e.g., KSRTC, APSRTC, TSRTC) by notification.
Corporation may provide road transport services, construct and manage passenger terminals, and maintain vehicles.
Corporations are self-financing entities; may borrow funds with State Government guarantee.
Corporations operate under permits granted under MVA 1988 Chapter VI. Special priority given to State Transport Undertakings on notified routes.
Employees of the Corporation are not government servants but have service conditions defined by the Corporation.

central_road_fund_act_2000.objective: To provide for the constitution of a Central Road Fund and to regulate the collection and application of cess on High Speed Diesel and Petrol for the development and maintenance of roads and highways.

key_provisions.description: Cess levied on every litre of High Speed Diesel and Petrol. Revenue credited to Central Road Fund.
Fund allocated to: National Highways, State Roads, Rural Roads (Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana), and railway over or under bridges.
Fund administered by Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
A portion of the fund is distributed to states for development of state roads.

central_road_fund_state_roads_rules_2007.short_title: The Central Road Fund (State Roads) Rules, 2007
central_road_fund_state_roads_rules_2007.objective: To prescribe the procedure and criteria for release of Central Road Fund money to States for development of state roads.

key_provisions.description: Funds distributed among states based on: (a) vehicle population, (b) road length, (c) geographical area.
Funds may be used for construction, upgradation and maintenance of state roads including bridges.
State PWD must submit project proposals to MoRTH for approval before fund utilisation.
States must submit utilisation certificates within 6 months of fund usage.
Accounts subject to audit by Comptroller and Auditor General of India.

no_fault_compensation.description: Payable by the owner/insurer without requiring proof of negligence or fault.

The claimant need not prove negligence for this amount.
Deductible from final MACT award if awarded subsequently.

telangana_provisions.title: Telangana Motor Vehicles Act and Rules
telangana_provisions.description: Telangana State follows the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 as the parent legislation, with state-specific rules under the Telangana Motor Vehicles Taxation Act and rules made by Telangana State Transport Authority (STA).

key_state_specific_provisions.description: Telangana levies One Time Tax (OTT) on all vehicles at the time of registration. Tax rates vary by vehicle type, engine capacity, and seating capacity.
Telangana levies a Green Tax on vehicles older than 15 years (for non-transport) and 10 years (for transport) at the time of fitness renewal.
Default speed limits in Telangana: Motorcycles and LMV — 50 km/h (urban), 65 km/h (highways); Transport vehicles — 65 km/h; Heavy vehicles — 40-50 km/h.
Telangana has 34 RTO offices. Code prefix: TS 01 (Hyderabad Central) through TS 36 (Narayanpet).
Telangana Traffic Police issues electronic challans (e-challans) through the Vahaan/Parivahan portal. Payment can be made online.
Hyderabad Traffic Police enforces additional restrictions: no-entry zones for HMVs in city centre during peak hours; specific parking zones; two-wheeler lane restrictions on ORR.

common_faqs.question: What is the fine for not wearing a helmet in India?
common_faqs.answer: Under Section 194D of the MVA 1988 (post 2019 amendment), the fine is Rs. 1,000. Additionally, the driving licence may be suspended for 3 months.

common_faqs.question: What is the fine for jumping a red light?
common_faqs.answer: Under Section 184(a) of the MVA 1988, the fine is Rs. 5,000 for the first offence and Rs. 10,000 for subsequent offences.

common_faqs.question: What is the fine for drunk driving in India?
common_faqs.answer: Under Section 185 of the MVA 1988, the fine is Rs. 10,000 for the first offence (and/or imprisonment up to 6 months) and Rs. 15,000 for subsequent offences (and/or imprisonment up to 2 years). The permissible BAC limit is 30 mg per 100 ml of blood.

common_faqs.question: What is the fine for driving without insurance?
common_faqs.answer: Under Section 196 of the MVA 1988, the fine is Rs. 2,000 for the first offence and Rs. 4,000 for subsequent offences.

common_faqs.question: What is the fine for driving without a licence?
common_faqs.answer: Under Section 181 of the MVA 1988, the fine is Rs. 5,000.

common_faqs.question: What is the fine for overspeeding?
common_faqs.answer: Under Section 183 of the MVA 1988, the fine is Rs. 2,000 for LMVs (cars) and Rs. 4,000 for HMVs/MMVs. Repeat offenders risk licence suspension.

common_faqs.question: What is the fine for using a mobile phone while driving?
common_faqs.answer: Under Section 184(c) of the MVA 1988, the fine is Rs. 5,000 for the first offence and Rs. 10,000 for subsequent offences. This is treated as dangerous driving.

common_faqs.question: What compensation is available in hit-and-run accident cases?
common_faqs.answer: Under the Compensation to Victims of Hit and Run Motor Accidents Scheme, 2022 (which replaced the Solatium Scheme 1989): Rs. 2,00,000 for death; Rs. 50,000 for grievous hurt. Apply to the Claims Enquiry Officer at the Taluka level.

common_faqs.question: Is it mandatory to carry vehicle documents while driving?
common_faqs.answer: Yes. Under Section 130 of the MVA 1988, you must carry: (1) Driving Licence, (2) Registration Certificate, (3) Insurance Certificate, (4) Fitness Certificate (for transport vehicles), (5) Permit (for transport vehicles). Documents can also be presented digitally via DigiLocker/mParivahan app.

common_faqs.question: What is the fine for not giving way to an ambulance?
common_faqs.answer: Under Section 194E of the MVA 1988, the fine for not providing way to emergency vehicles (ambulance, fire service) is Rs. 10,000.
